name: Iraq War
description: US-led invasion toppled Saddam Hussein and dismantled the Iraqi state, triggering years of sectarian warfare and insurgency. Destroyed Iraq's infrastructure and delayed any north-south transit corridor development for two decades. Kept Hormuz under permanent threat as Iran exploited the power vacuum. The chaos made the Iraq Development Road concept impossible until post-ISIS stabilization.

name: Syrian Civil War
description: Multi-sided civil war that shattered Syria as a transit state and drew in every major power. Severed the northern land bridge between Turkey, Iraq, and the Mediterranean. Blocked BRI's planned overland route through the Levant. Turkey's involvement and the Kurdish corridor question make any east-west land trade route through northern Syria/Iraq politically impossible without resolution.

name: Yemen Civil War / Houthi Campaign
description: Iran-backed Houthi movement seized much of Yemen including the capital Sana'a, triggering Saudi-led intervention. The war gave the Houthis control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline, enabling them to threaten the Bab el-Mandab strait. By 2023-2024, Houthi anti-ship missile and drone attacks effectively closed the southern Red Sea to commercial shipping, forcing reroutes around the Cape of Good Hope and directly threatening the IMEC corridor's viability.

name: Libyan Civil Wars
description: NATO intervention toppled Gaddafi in 2011, plunging Libya into state collapse and recurring civil war. Two rival governments and hundreds of militias turned Libya into a failed state on the Mediterranean's southern shore. Disrupted Mediterranean shipping lanes, created a migration crisis affecting European port security, and opened the door for Russian Wagner Group expansion in North Africa. Libya's oil exports remain intermittent.

name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
description: 44-day war in which Azerbaijan, backed by Turkish drones and advisors, recaptured most of Nagorno-Karabakh from Armenian forces. The war reshaped Caucasus power dynamics and opened discussion of the Zangezur corridor connecting Azerbaijan to its Nakhchivan exclave through southern Armenia. This directly affects INSTC routing through the Caucasus and Iran's northern border security. Russian peacekeepers deployed but influence waned.

name: Azerbaijan Takeover of Nagorno-Karabakh
description: Azerbaijan launched a one-day military operation in September 2023, forcing the dissolution of the Nagorno-Karabakh republic and the complete exodus of its 120,000 ethnic Armenian population. Completed Azerbaijan's territorial reconquest and strengthened Turkey-Azerbaijan's position on the Caucasus corridor. Weakened Russia's role as regional security guarantor. Accelerated talks on alternative INSTC routings that bypass Armenian territory entirely.

name: Israel-Gaza War
description: Hamas launched a mass attack on southern Israel on October 7, 2023, triggering a full-scale Israeli military campaign in Gaza. The war derailed the IMEC corridor agreement signed weeks earlier at the G20, as Arab states suspended normalization talks. Triggered Houthi Red Sea attacks in solidarity, effectively closing the Bab el-Mandab. The conflict made IMEC's planned Haifa terminus politically toxic for Saudi Arabia and other Arab corridor partners.

name: Israel-Hezbollah / Lebanon War
description: Hezbollah opened a front against Israel in solidarity with Hamas starting October 2023, escalating through 2024 into a full air and ground campaign. Israel's strikes decimated Hezbollah's leadership and military infrastructure. The northern front war disrupted Mediterranean shipping near Haifa and raised insurance premiums across the eastern Mediterranean. Directly threatened IMEC's Israeli port nodes and demonstrated Iran's ability to activate multi-front pressure on corridor chokepoints.

name: Russia-Ukraine War
description: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 shattered European energy security and severed BRI's primary overland rail route through Russia/Belarus to Europe. Blocked Black Sea grain exports for months, militarized the Bosphorus under the Montreux Convention, and triggered a wholesale reorientation of global trade flows. European sanctions on Russia forced BRI freight onto longer Central Asian and maritime routes. The war accelerated the Middle Corridor (Trans-Caspian) as a Russia-bypass route.

name: Ethiopia-Tigray War
parties: Ethiopian Federal Government + Eritrea + Amhara militias
description: Devastating civil war in northern Ethiopia between federal forces (allied with Eritrea) and the TPLF. One of the deadliest conflicts of the 21st century. Destabilized the Horn of Africa, threatened Djibouti's port operations as a logistics hub, and complicated Ethiopia's access to the sea through Eritrean and Djiboutian ports. Eritrea's involvement raised tensions near the Bab el-Mandab. Ceasefire in November 2022, but the war exposed the fragility of Horn of Africa trade infrastructure.

name: Somalia / Al-Shabaab Insurgency
description: Al-Shabaab insurgency has prevented Somali state consolidation for nearly two decades. Controls large rural areas and conducts attacks in Mogadishu. The instability blocks development of Somali ports (Mogadishu, Kismayo) as viable trade nodes and keeps the western Indian Ocean a high-risk shipping zone. Berbera port in Somaliland (backed by DP World/UAE) serves as the only functional corridor anchor in the region, but lacks hinterland security.

name: Balochistan Insurgency / CPEC Attacks
description: Baloch separatist groups have waged a persistent insurgency in Pakistan's largest and poorest province, directly targeting China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) infrastructure. Attacks on Chinese workers, engineers, and Gwadar port facilities have repeatedly delayed CPEC completion. The BLA specifically targets Chinese nationals to raise the cost of BRI investment. Gwadar port, meant to be BRI's Indian Ocean anchor, operates far below capacity due to security constraints and local opposition.

name: Iran-Israel Shadow War
description: Escalating covert and overt conflict between Iran and Israel spanning multiple theaters. Spanning covert operations since 2010 (Stuxnet, scientist assassinations), escalating to Iran's April 2024 direct missile/drone attack on Israel marked the first open interstate strike. Israel's assassination of IRGC and Hezbollah commanders, combined with Iran's Hormuz closure threats, places the entire IMEC corridor at existential risk. Iran's proxy network (Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias) can simultaneously threaten multiple IMEC nodes. The shadow war is the single largest systemic risk to corridor construction.

name: Sudan Civil War
description: Full-scale civil war erupted in April 2023 between Sudan's two military factions, destroying Khartoum and spreading across Darfur and central Sudan. Created the world's largest displacement crisis. Port Sudan on the Red Sea became the de facto capital, raising its strategic significance. The war destabilizes the entire Red Sea western littoral, complicates Egypt's southern security, and adds another failed state to the corridor of instability stretching from Libya to Somalia.

name: Myanmar Civil War
description: Following the February 2021 military coup, Myanmar descended into nationwide civil war. Ethnic armed organizations and new People's Defense Forces control large portions of the country, including areas along China's planned BRI overland corridor to the Indian Ocean. The China-Myanmar Economic Corridor (CMEC), including the Kyaukphyu deep-sea port and oil/gas pipelines, faces severe security risks. Myanmar was meant to give China a Malacca bypass; instead it became a conflict zone.

name: Afghanistan War / Taliban Takeover
description: Two decades of US-led war ended with the Taliban's return to power in August 2021. Afghanistan's instability blocked INSTC's eastern branch through Central Asia and prevented any overland connectivity between South and Central Asia. Under Taliban rule, Afghanistan remains isolated from international trade frameworks. The Wakhan Corridor connection to China and the Chabahar-Afghanistan rail link to INSTC remain unrealized. Afghanistan is a permanent gap in Eurasian connectivity.

name: ISIS / Islamic State Campaigns
description: ISIS seized vast territory across Iraq and Syria in 2014, declaring a caliphate that straddled the planned Iraq Development Road route. Destroyed infrastructure, displaced millions, and drew in a US-led air campaign. The ISIS threat in the Sinai also endangered Suez Canal security. Although the territorial caliphate was defeated by 2019, ISIS sleeper cells remain active along the Iraq-Syria border, and the destruction set back Iraqi infrastructure development by a decade.

name: Sahel Conflicts / Wagner Expansion
description: A cascade of military coups in Mali (2020, 2021), Burkina Faso (2022), and Niger (2023) expelled French forces and invited Russian Wagner/Africa Corps mercenaries. Jihadi insurgencies by al-Qaeda and ISIS affiliates continue expanding. The Sahel belt of instability blocks any trans-African trade corridor and pushes migration pressure toward Mediterranean routes. China's BRI investments in West African ports (Lome, Conakry, Kribi) face hinterland insecurity. Russia's mercenary presence adds a geopolitical overlay to what was already a humanitarian catastrophe.

name: Iran-backed Iraqi Militia Proxy War
description: Iranian-backed militias in Iraq conduct persistent attacks on US bases and have increasingly targeted commercial and energy infrastructure. The Hashd al-Shaabi (Popular Mobilization Forces) act as a parallel military force that gives Iran de facto veto power over Iraqi infrastructure projects, including the Iraq Development Road. Any corridor transiting Iraq must account for militia-controlled territory. These groups also serve as a pressure valve Iran can activate to threaten Hormuz-adjacent shipping and Gulf state security.

name: Red Sea / Houthi Shipping War
description: Beginning in November 2023, Houthi forces launched sustained anti-ship missile, drone, and naval mine attacks against commercial vessels in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Major shipping lines (Maersk, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd) rerouted around the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days and $1M+ per voyage. Suez Canal revenues dropped over 50%. The attacks are the most direct threat to IMEC's viability, as the corridor requires safe passage through the Bab el-Mandab. US/UK airstrikes on Houthi positions failed to stop the campaign, demonstrating non-state actors' ability to close a global chokepoint.

name: South China Sea Confrontations
casualty_estimate: Low — primarily vessel ramming, water cannon, and standoffs
description: China's militarization of artificial islands and aggressive coast guard operations across the South China Sea. Regular confrontations at Second Thomas Shoal (Philippines), Scarborough Shoal, and Paracel/Spratly Islands. US Navy conducts freedom of navigation operations. $5.3 trillion in trade transits annually. Any escalation over Taiwan would close the sea entirely.

name: Somali Piracy Crisis
parties: International naval coalitions (CMF, EU NAVFOR, China Navy)
description: Somali piracy peaked 2008-2012 with 200+ attacks per year in the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. Triggered multinational naval deployments including China's first overseas naval mission (2008). Gave China the operational justification for its Djibouti naval base (2017). International naval patrols largely suppressed piracy by 2013, but the crisis reshaped maritime security architecture in the Indian Ocean.
